clusters.name: Deficits in intellectual functions (Criterion A)
items: Deficits in reasoning and problem solving (DSM p.37)
Deficits in planning and abstract thinking (DSM p.37)
Deficits in judgment and academic learning (DSM p.37)
Deficits in learning from experience confirmed by clinical assessment and standardized testing (DSM p.37)

clusters.name: Deficits in adaptive functioning (Criterion B)
items: Failure to meet developmental and sociocultural standards for personal independence (DSM p.38)
Failure to meet standards for social responsibility (DSM p.38)
Limited functioning in one or more activities of daily life across multiple environments (DSM p.38)

criteria.thresholds: All three criteria (A, B, and C) must be met, with onset during the developmental period (DSM p.38)

epidemiology.prevalence: ID: 1%-3% of child/adolescent population (Dulcan p.116). Down Syndrome: ~1 in 1,000 live births (Dulcan p.119). Fragile X Syndrome: 14 per 100,000 males (Dulcan p.120)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: ID is more common in males: 1.6:1 M:F for mild ID, 1.2:1 M:F for severe ID (DSM p.44); 20% more males overall (Dulcan p.116)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: ID onset is during the developmental period (DSM p.38). Down Syndrome features are congenital and present at birth (Dulcan p.119)
epidemiology.heritability: Fragile X is the leading cause of inherited ID (Dulcan p.120); Down Syndrome is typically sporadic due to meiotic nondisjunction of maternal origin (Dulcan p.119)
comorbidities: ASD in ~25% of Fragile X patients (Dulcan p.120)
ADHD in Fragile X patients (Dulcan p.120)
Alzheimer's disease in Down Syndrome (DSM p.371, Dulcan p.119)
Congenital heart defects in 40%-50% of Down Syndrome (Dulcan p.119)
epidemiology.prognosis: Alzheimer's pathology develops in nearly 100% of Down Syndrome patients past age 40 (DSM p.371, Dulcan p.119). Fragile X features worsen after puberty (Dulcan p.120)

etiology.genetic: Down Syndrome: Trisomy 21 due to meiotic nondisjunction of maternal origin (Dulcan p.119). Fragile X Syndrome: >200 CGG trinucleotide repeats in FMR1 gene causing hypermethylation and silencing (Dulcan p.120)
etiology.neurobiology: Down: overexpression of APP on chromosome 21 causing beta-amyloid plaques (DSM p.373, StahlNeuro p.496). Fragile X: absence of FMRP protein causing altered synaptic plasticity (Dulcan p.120)
etiology.environmental: Advanced maternal age is a risk factor for meiotic nondisjunction in Down Syndrome (DSM p.137, Dulcan p.119). Prenatal toxin exposure (e.g., FASD) in ID (Dulcan p.118)

first_line: Multidisciplinary behavioral, educational, and speech therapies (Dulcan p.112, p.119-120)
Risperidone and Aripiprazole (FDA approved) for severe irritability, aggression, and self-injury (Dulcan p.126-127)
Stimulants (Methylphenidate, Amphetamine) as first-line for comorbid ADHD (Dulcan p.128)
second_line: Minocycline (25-100 mg/day) for anxiety and mood symptoms in Fragile X Syndrome (Dulcan p.127)
Guanfacine (up to 3 mg/day) or Clonidine for ADHD symptoms in ID (Dulcan p.128)
Valproic acid for ADHD and behavioral symptoms in Fragile X boys (Dulcan p.127)
key_side_effects: Significant metabolic side effects and weight gain from atypical antipsychotics (Dulcan p.820, StahlKids p.46)
Sedation, syncope, and bradycardia from alpha-2 agonists (StahlKids p.139, p.248)
Worsening of anxiety, crying, and hyperarousal with stimulants in ID (Dulcan p.128)
treatment.monitoring: Metabolic screening (weight, BMI, fasting lipids, glucose) for atypical antipsychotics (Dulcan p.820). Baseline ECG for cardiac abnormalities prior to stimulant/alpha-agonist use (Dulcan p.525, p.744). Growth/height monitoring for stimulants (StahlKids p.11). TSH/Free T4 monitoring every 6 months for lithium (StahlKids p.291).

items: WISC-V for children aged 6 to 16 years, 11 months (Dulcan p.113)
WPPSI-IV for children aged 2 years, 6 months to 7 years, 3 months (Dulcan p.113)
SB-5 for individuals aged 2 to 85+ years (Dulcan p.113)
Leiter-3 as a completely nonverbal intelligence test (DSM p.59, Dulcan p.113)
Vineland-3 for adaptive behavior assessment (Dulcan p.114)
key_numbers: 15 to 20 percent of high school students report serious suicidal thoughts annually (StahlKids p.11)
2 to 7 is the NNT for acute risperidone/aripiprazole response in autism-related irritability (Dulcan p.809)
11 subdomains of adaptive behavior are assessed in ABAS-3 (Dulcan p.114)

items: Rett syndrome (MECP2 mutation) mimicking ASD with regression between ages 1 and 4 years (DSM p.66, Dulcan p.120)
Inborn errors of metabolism (IEM) mimicking developmental delay, or presenting with regression or acute psychosis (Dulcan p.121)
Hypothyroidism mimicking psychomotor slowing, fatigue, and depression (DSM p.208, Dulcan p.1095)
key_numbers: 1 to 4 years is the typical age range of regression in Rett syndrome (DSM p.66, Dulcan p.120)
10 percent or more of ID cases may be caused by biochemical genetic/metabolic disorders (Dulcan p.117)
2 percent to 14 percent of ID cases are caused by inborn errors of metabolism (Dulcan p.121)

items: Down Syndrome facial dysmorphology: flat facial profile, upward slanting palpebral fissures, epicanthal folds, and macroglossia (Dulcan p.119)
Down Syndrome physical findings: short stature, hypotonia, single palmar crease, and hyperlax joints (Dulcan p.119)
Down Syndrome anomalies: congenital heart defects (AVSD) and digestive tract malformations like duodenal atresia (Dulcan p.119)
Fragile X Syndrome facial features: long and narrow face, prominent forehead, prognathism, and large, prominent ears (Dulcan p.120)
Fragile X Syndrome physical features: postpubertal macro-orchidism, hyperlax joints, and pes planus (DSM p.71, Dulcan p.120)
key_numbers: 80 features or more characterize the phenotype of Down Syndrome (Dulcan p.119)
40 percent to 50 percent of Down Syndrome patients have congenital heart defects (Dulcan p.119)
100 percent of Down Syndrome patients develop Alzheimer's neuropathological changes by age 40 (DSM p.371, Dulcan p.119)
200 CGG repeats or more defines the full mutation of FMR1 in Fragile X (Dulcan p.120)
25 percent of Fragile X individuals meet the criteria for ASD (Dulcan p.120)
80 percent or more of postpubertal Fragile X males exhibit macro-orchidism (Dulcan p.120)
25 mL is the testicular volume threshold for postpubertal macro-orchidism (Dulcan p.120)

high_yield: Rosa's Law (Public Law 111-256) replaced all federal references to 'mental retardation' with 'intellectual disability' on October 5, 2010 (DSM p.38, Dulcan p.107).
DSM-5-TR determines the severity of Intellectual Disability (ID) by adaptive functioning rather than IQ score cutoffs (DSM p.42, Dulcan p.107).
Fragile X is the leading cause of inherited intellectual disability and the most common single-gene cause of Autism Spectrum Disorder (Dulcan p.120).

Nearly 100% of individuals with Down syndrome who survive past age 40 show the neuropathological plaques and tangles of Alzheimer's disease due to APP overexpression on chromosome 21 (DSM p.371, p.373, Dulcan p.119).
Every child with ASD or global developmental delay should receive genetic screening for Fragile X syndrome (Dulcan p.120, p.145).
Lithium treatment can induce hypothyroidism in pediatric patients, which requires active monitoring of TSH and Free T4 every 6 months (StahlKids p.291).
Aripiprazole at a mean dose of 9.8 mg/day significantly improves irritability and self-injurious behavior in Fragile X syndrome (Dulcan p.126-127).
Valproate treatment can cause hyperammonemic encephalopathy without abnormal liver enzymes, presenting as acute cognitive slowing or lethargy (StahlKids p.472).
